title: South Korea vs Japan: Which Should You Visit?
description: A data-backed comparison of South Korea and Japan based on Reddit discussions, real costs, food scenes, culture, and traveler preferences.

categories.title: 🍜 Food & Dining
categories.summary: This is probably the most hotly debated category between the two countries, and it comes down to what you value:variety and refinement (Japan)orbold flavors and social dining (Korea).

categories.summary: South Korea is cheaper than Japan across almost every category. The weak yen has narrowed the gap in 2025-2026, but Korea still wins — especially for food, alcohol, and accommodation. Here's a realistic daily budget breakdown:

categories.title: 🚇 Getting Around
categories.summary: Both countries have world-class public transit, but with very different strengths and pain points.

categories.title: 🌸 Best Time to Visit
categories.summary: Both countries have four distinct seasons with similar climate patterns, but Seoul is notably colder in winter and hotter in summer than Tokyo due to its more continental climate.

categories.title: 🏨 Where to Stay
categories.summary: Myeongdong— Tourist central. Shopping, street food, skincare stores everywhere. Central location, easy metro access. Can feel touristy but incredibly convenient.

categories.title: 🎒 Day Trips
categories.summary: Japan has a decisive edge here simply because the country is larger and more geographically diverse. But Korea's day trips from Seoul pack a punch.

categories.title: ✈️ Why Not Both?
categories.summary: Seoul and Tokyo are only2.5 hours apart by plane, and budget carriers (Peach Aviation, Jeju Air, T'way, Jin Air) frequently offer fares as low as $80–150 one way. Many travelers combine both countries in a single 2–3 week trip, and the contrast between the two makes each feel more distinct.

faqs.question: Is South Korea or Japan better for first-time visitors to Asia?
faqs.answer: Japan is generally recommended for first-time visitors to Asia. Reddit overwhelmingly favors Japan for its deeper variety of experiences — temples, food diversity, nature, pop culture, and world-class transit. Japan also has more English signage and a more established tourist infrastructure. However

faqs.question: Is South Korea cheaper than Japan?
faqs.answer: Yes, South Korea is generally cheaper than Japan. Hotels in Seoul run 50,000-120,000 won per night ($35-85) for mid-range vs 10,000-20,000 yen ($70-140) in Tokyo. faqs.question: How long should I spend in South Korea vs Japan?
faqs.answer: Japan has far more geographic spread and variety — most travelers recommend 10-14 days to cover Tokyo, Kyoto, Osaka, and a few day trips. faqs.answer: This is the most debated question on Reddit, and it genuinely comes down to personal preference. faqs.answer: South Korea wins for nightlife, and it's not particularly close.
